question: Which Veda contains the maximum number of verses?
solution:
The correct answer is __**"Rig Veda".**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rig Veda** is the oldest form of Veda. 
 
• It is the **oldest **known Vedic Sanskrit text.
 
• 'Rigveda' means praise knowledge.
 
• It has 10600 verses, and 1028 hymns called **'Suktas'.**
 
• It also has a collection of 10 books known as **'Mandalas'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are** four Vedas** in Sanskrit:

 
 
• Rigveda
 
• Samaveda
 
• Yajurveda
 
• Atharvaveda
 
 
 
• **Samaveda -** It is called the Veda of melodies and chants. There are two Upanishads in Samaveda. This Veda is considered the root of Indian classical dance and music.
 
• **Yajurveda - **This means worship knowledge. It has two types- Krishna and Shukla. It contains ritual-performing mantras.
 
• **Atharvaveda - **This Veda contains daily life routines. It is called as Veda of magical formulas. This contains three primary Upanishads.
